summary.intent: Resolve open PR review comments on PR #416, then after merging update project documentation (DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, README.md, and a new filesystem spec) on a docs branch to reflect the state after phases 28-37.
summary.outcome: All 4 review threads were triaged, 2 code fixes and 1 doc fix were committed and pushed, threads replied to and resolved. A docs PR (#419) was created with updated DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, README.md, and a new FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md; the web worker encryption todo was moved to done; and DEFERRED.md was further cleaned up to remove already-implemented, out-of-scope, and premature items.

repo: Grafana Faro (not Sentry) is the live error tracking solution, implemented in apps/web/src/lib/faro.ts.
FUSE write-op coverage is intentionally not unit-tested due to host-OS mocking complexity; coverage comes from the Desktop E2E suite instead. This is a deliberate architectural choice, not a gap.
Session replay is explicitly out-of-scope as an anti-feature for a zero-knowledge privacy product.
Production Kubo hardening is premature — no production environment exists yet.
Batch upload is implemented in the JS SDK and web app but NOT in the Rust SDK.

The 'lazy file reading' issue (useDropUpload.ts:140) was independently flagged by both CodeRabbit (phase 37 review round 1) and GitHub Copilot — it's tracked as a deferred item requiring an SDK API contract change to accept File objects or read callbacks instead of Uint8Array.
Web Worker encryption (Phase 37) was shipped but the corresponding todo file was never moved from .planning/todos/pending/ to done/ — required a manual cleanup step.
The project uses release-please for versioning; manifest is at .release-please-manifest.json.

code.finding: getWorker() and postMessage() can throw, leaking entries from the pending map. Fix: wrap in try/catch and clean up pending entry on error.
Batch reads all files to memory before passing to SDK — architectural limitation since SDK accepts Uint8Array not File objects. Deferred; requires SDK contract change.
uploadFiles() doc comment overstated memory bounding guarantees; corrected to accurately describe concurrency-pool behavior.

workflow: Use gh api graphql with resolveReviewThread mutation to batch-resolve PR review threads.
When replying to PR review comments via REST, use --field (not -f) for in_reply_to since it must be an integer.
Integration tests that require a live backend will fail in CI/local without a running server — distinguish these from unit test failures before acting on them.
After a PR merges, always check pending todos for items that were implemented in the merged work and move them to done/.
When auditing a deferred items list, cross-check against actual codebase state — items can silently become implemented, out-of-scope, or premature without the list being updated.

friction: The web worker encryption todo was left in pending/ after Phase 37 shipped it — required a separate discovery and manual move step.

DEFERRED.md contained stale/incorrect entries: error tracking already implemented as Faro, session replay never in scope, production Kubo hardening premature — required a second audit pass after initial update.
CONCERNS.md had a misleading entry about FUSE lacking automated tests, which required clarification and a 'won't fix' annotation.
git commit with parentheses in the message failed (likely shell quoting issue); had to retry with dashes instead.
open_items: Lazy file reading in useDropUpload.ts — requires SDK API change to accept File objects or read callbacks instead of Uint8Array (tracked in DEFERRED.md, originally CodeRabbit thread 8).
Batch upload not implemented in Rust SDK — noted in FEATURES.md feature matrix.
All remaining deferred items in .planning/DEFERRED.md across Upload Pipeline, Observability, Code Quality, and Infra Hardening categories.
E2E test coverage for Desktop FUSE components is via Desktop E2E suite only — no unit tests by design, but suite coverage should be maintained as FUSE plumbing evolves.
docs/FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md documents 5 cross-platform gaps (case sensitivity, reserved names, path length, etc.) that may need resolution as the desktop client matures on Windows.
